issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text specify an abstract Animal constructor with two parameters (Animal(String, int)) and an age attribute, but both the provided template Main usage and the solution implement Animal and its subclasses with a single-argument constructor (String name) and no age attribute. This inconsistency between the specification and the actual code (template and solution) will confuse students about which constructor and attributes they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to define Animal with only a name attribute and a single-argument constructor Animal(String) (and remove age references), matching the template Main usage and the solution; or (B) update the template and solution to include the age attribute and two-argument constructors (Animal(String, int)) and adjust all subclass constructors and the example Main accordingly. Ensure getters/setters and tests align with the chosen design.
